headline: Directed city clerk to note that cannabis ordinance 12.12.190 is invalidated and under review, pending a new draft.
summary: The committee discussed how to rewrite MCC 12.12.190 after a court ruling invalidated it, including whether the Planning Board or City Council should grant special permits for marijuana facilities. No final decision was made on that question. The committee approved the March 10, 2026 minutes as amended and voted to have the City Clerk note in Municode that 12.12.190 is invalidated and under review while Councillor Winslow prepares a new draft for the next meeting.
decisions: Amended the March 10, 2026 committee minutes to add the word 'section' after 'entire ordinance' - unanimous vote.
Approved the March 10, 2026 committee minutes as amended - unanimous vote.
Directed the City Clerk to note in Municode that MCC 12.12.190 has been invalidated and is under review - motion passed unanimously.

## Business

**156-26** 

In accordance with the Order numbered 137-26 Committee will meet to begin discussion on draft amendments to MCC 12.12.190 necessary to comply with the Court Judgement rendered in Benevolent Botanicals v City of Malden.

Sponsors: Stephen Winslow Attachments: Structured Analysis from O'Malley

2022 Cannabis amendments recap from McDonald

Judgement - Main Points from Winslow

Memo Cannabis Directive v4 March 19 2026

Romero's Comments on March 19 Memo

Discussion on this paper began with Building Commissioner Nelson Miller noting that although Judge Rubin had invalidated MCC 12.12.190, the court ruling did not address MCC 12.12.030 Use Regulations, which mandates the special permitting process for marijuana facilities. Additionally, MCC 12.12.010 places the special permit granting authority for marijuana licenses with the City Council as opposed to the Planning Board. These additional ordinance citations were not mentioned in the court's ruling, therefore all special permit criteria still exists.

Commissioner Miller is of the opinion there are two main questions to be considered first and foremost. Does the Council want to keep the special permit requirement for marijuana licenses and if so, do they wish to keep that authority with the Council or transfer the granting authority to the Planning Board? And then, to decide which, if any, parts of 12.12.190 they wish to reinstate, such as state mandated school buffer zones, and which will be completely re-written.

Because the court ruling didn't touch on the special permitting process, and for the sake of consistency, Councillor Linehan is of the opinion the granting authority should stay under the authority of the Council at this time. After some discussion on the pros and cons of doing so, Councillor Colon Hayes is leaning towards transferring the granting authority to the Planning Board.

Councillor Crowe is agreeable to transferring the granting authority because the laws, stigma, and controversy of marijuana has changed in recent years and so now the special permit is no different than any other that would normally come before the Planning Board. Historically, the City Council has been the granting authority for permits that had the potential to be more political or controversial with higher impact to the neighborhoods. Examples include storage facilities and structures over six stories. In such cases, the Council has direct accountability to constituents while the Planning Board may be less influenced by public opinion.

Buffer zones for school zone are still mandated by state law. Buffer zones for all other reasons must now be reconsidered, for example substance abuse treatment centers. Councillor O'Malley read from M.G.L. c. 94g s. 5(b)(3) that states a city may adopt an ordinance to reduce the distance requirement to less than 500 feet around schools. Clarity should also be written on if the granting authority has the ability to grant relief from these zones.

Moving forward, the committee will begin with a new draft of 12.12.190 then send that to a joint session of the Planning Board with Rules and Ordinance for a public hearing.

A motion was made by Councillor Colon Hayes, seconded by Councillor Crowe, that the City Clerk will notate in Municode that 12.12.190 has been invalidated and is currently under review. Motion passed unanimously.

For the next meeting, Councillor Winslow will prepare a draft for the committee's consideration.
